why: A proper subset of {1,2,3,4} is any subset except {1,2,3,4} itself, and being a superset of {3} just means containing the element 3 (equality is allowed, so {3} itself qualifies); there are 2^3 = 8 subsets containing 3, minus the full set, giving 7, confirmed by exhaustive enumeration of all 16 subsets. The other options are the alternative-reading distractors — 8 counts all supersets of {3} without dropping the full set, and 6 comes from reading 'superset' as strict and excluding {3} itself — and all four option values (5, 6, 7, 8) are distinct, so no two can denote the same quantity.
